hook_text: Every December, buses and taxis leave the cities packed with people going home to their villages. Why did they leave in the first place?
clip_script: A village in the Eastern Cape: green hills, cattle, a few houses far apart, a long walk to the clinic, few jobs. Cape Town: crowds, traffic, shops, hospitals, factories and offices. Lindiwe's family moved for work and better schools. Moving from rural areas to towns and cities is called urbanisation. Push factors drive people out; pull factors draw them in. About two out of three South Africans now live in urban areas.
visual_style: Whiteboard split scene: a quiet village with cattle on the left, a busy city skyline on the right, and arrows labelled push and pull carrying people across.
mood: Warm and personal, balancing hope and difficulty.
pacing: A personal story, then a clear comparison of rural and urban, then push and pull factors.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make a table of three push factors and three pull factors.
